name: Collins 2013 Shiva amygdaloid: CCW 100->240 ms, 4-s gaps (20 min)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Collins & Persinger 2013; Collins 2013 MA thesis), on Todd Murphy's 64-coil Shiva hat
summary: The 20-min field condition of Collins & Persinger 2013: Shiva's amygdaloid signal, rebuilt (289 points of 3 ms, then 4 s of silence), stepped counter-clockwise around the head, 100 ms on the left frontal position and 20 ms longer on each next one. The thesis reports more out-of-body, 'somewhere else' and presence items than in a sham group (5 against 4 people) and no rise in temporal delta power under the field.
notes: Source: a hat with 64 solenoids in 8 columns of 8, 45 degrees apart, over the left and right frontal, temporal, parietal and occipital lobes, the first column left frontal (Saroka 2010 p.4 [469], p.5 [470]). The pattern stayed 100 ms on the left frontal column and 20 ms longer on each next column, counter-clockwise from the top; it had 289 points of 3 ms, with 4000 ms between cycles (Collins 2014 p.40 [31]). This program plays one coil per column on the ring Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2. Each source column ran from the top of the skull to its side (Saroka 2010 p.5 [470]); one coil near the rim stands for it, so the upper part of every column is not driven. The signal is rebuilt: the thesis gives only the point count, 3 ms and a range of -5 to +5 V (p.40 [31]), and the point values were never published as numbers. The project's rising sweep (6-30 Hz) with that point duration and length stands in. The thesis does not say how the 867-ms pattern and its 4-s pause were lined up with the 1.36-s turn; here the rotation runs without stopping, an assumption. The thesis states about 1 uT (10 mG) inside the head, with no instrument and no place of measurement (p.40 [31]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Support: 9 volunteers (5 field, 4 sham), told they might or might not get a field; field subjects endorsed 35 % against 9 % of 20 exit items. Experimenter blinding is not reported, the endpoints are self-reports, and nobody has repeated it. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). murphy-shiva64-obe-lab is the 5-min single case of Saroka et al. 2010 on the same hat. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on fear, headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated in a comfortable chair in a quiet, dark room (originally a shielded acoustic chamber), eyes closed for the whole 20 min. The lab took 30-s EEG samples before the field and at 5, 10, 15 and 20 min, and gave a 20-item exit questionnaire afterwards.
schedule: One 20-min session in the original. For a self-test, use the app's Blind option so the helmet picks field or sham, and fill in the questionnaire before the result is revealed.
source: Collins & Persinger 2013, Changing velocity circumcerebral magnetic fields produce altered state experiences and lowered delta-theta power over the temporal lobes, Review of Psychology Frontier 2(2):26-29 ; Collins 2013, Quantitative differences in participants exposed to patterned, weak-intensity electromagnetic fields: investigating the Shiva, MA thesis (Psychology), Laurentian University, ch. 2 https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/c03e0259-4b31-410f-9552-d90c9c2b81a4/content ; Saroka, Mulligan, Murphy & Persinger 2010, NeuroQuantology 8(4):466-477 https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275606923_Experimental_Elicitation_of_an_Out_of_Body_Experience_and_Concomitant_Cross-Hemispheric_Electroencephalographic_Coherence ; Murphy, Shiva coil locations https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/shiva/shiva_demo/locations.htm ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
